title.narrative: The lake Albert oil inter-region pilot project

description.narrative:
The exploration and mining of oil in Lake Albert in Western Uganda and Eastern DRC brings in challenges of justice and oil governance in both countries as well as brings in the reality that CAFOD partners in Bunia and Hoima diocese must address in the quest of better governance,especially in the management of the oil resource as part of and in support of the already ongong governace activities supported by the ABG programme across the two regions.In February 2012, the Action for Better Governance (ABG) programme organized a three day workshop in Nairobi. The Purpose of that workshop was to bring the ABG implementing partners in DRC and Uganda working around Lake Albert on activities related to oil mining to; reach a common understanding of the issues related to oil development in Lake Albert and agree to implement a prioritized set of joint actions in response. This is a pilot project by CAFOD under the ABG programme and part of an ongoing governance programme to bring together partners from two countries working on a common justice issues related to the activities of oil mining across and along the national borders of DRC and Uganda so as to ensure better engagement with local communities. Specifically this pilot project was borne out of initial conversations that explored possible joint programming between CAFOD’s implementing partners in Uganda and DRC on governance issues related to oil mining and development on Lake Albert in Uganda and DRC.
the lake Albert oil activities shall be implemented by the partners in DRC and Uganda jointly from October 2012 to March 2013 by CAFOD partners. In Uganda the NCCJP and the diocese of Hoima shall be responsible for the management of the activities while in DRC ,CDC,CDJP,Haki Ameni and CERN shall be responsible for the activities.
